topic: Earthquake at home: run to the doorway or get under the table?
title: Earthquake At Home
idea: The doorway is an old myth; drop, cover and hold on where you are.
hook: The floor starts shaking. Doorway, or under the table?

beats.line: To reach the doorway, you cross the room while it shakes.
beats.see: Card A DOORWAY highlighted; the character staggers across a tilting living room floor toward the door frame. Stagger on 'cross', room wobbles on 'shakes'.

beats.line: A bookshelf comes down right where you were walking.
beats.see: A tall bookshelf topples and books rain onto the spot the character just left. Crash on 'down'.

beats.line: Most injuries come from moving during the shaking, or from falling things.
beats.see: Two icons stamp onto screen: a walking figure and a falling lamp, each with an injury mark. Walker on 'moving', lamp on 'falling'.

beats.line: And in a modern home, a doorway is no stronger than the rest.
beats.see: X ray view of the wall: the door frame has the same thin studs as the wall beside it; a MYTH stamp lands on card A. Studs on 'modern', stamp on 'stronger'.

beats.line: The table wins. Drop, cover, hold on.
beats.see: Card B TABLE gets a green check; three quick icons flash: knees, table, hands gripping a leg. Check on 'table', icons on 'Drop', 'cover', 'hold'.

beats.line: One. Drop onto your hands and knees.
beats.see: Step card 1 DROP; character drops to all fours as the floor jolts. Drop on 'Drop'.

beats.line: Two. Get under a sturdy table and cover your head and neck.
beats.see: Step card 2 COVER; character crawls under the table, one arm over head and neck, a vase smashes on the tabletop above. Crawl on 'under', smash on 'cover'.

beats.line: Three. Hold on until the shaking stops.
beats.see: Step card 3 HOLD ON; the table slides a little and the character slides with it, gripping a leg, until the room goes still. Grip on 'Hold', stillness on 'stops'.

end.line: Next shake, you're under the table, not in the doorway.
end.see: The floor jolts again as in the hook; this time the character is already under the table while the empty doorway gets a red X. Jolt on 'shake', X on 'doorway', loops into the hook.

description: Earthquake at home: run for the doorway or get under the table? The doorway is an old myth.

facts.claim: Do not stand in a doorway: in modern homes doorways are no stronger than the rest of the house. Do not run outside or to another room during shaking.
Most injuries come from falling and flying objects and from people trying to move during the shaking.
facts.source: McBride et al., USGS-led study (as listed in FACTS-batch-035-046.md; snippet, no number used)

facts.claim: Drop onto hands and knees, Cover head and neck (under a sturdy table if one is near), Hold on until the shaking stops.

notes: Correct card: B TABLE. The FACTS file has no usable number for this topic (injury study is snippet only, Northridge numbers are AVOID), so this video has no stake number; the stake beat is 'most injuries come from moving or falling things'. The bookshelf falling is a dramatization of that fact, not a claim. Hook implies a table is nearby, which matches 'under a sturdy table if one is near'. Did not include the in-bed rule or the triangle of life to stay in the word budget. 'X ray' written without hyphen in see only.
